description.p: Alexandria is a GTK4 library for managing scientific papers. Point it at a directory of PDFs and it extracts metadata (title, authors, year, DOI, journal) from XMP, page text, CrossRef and OpenAlex, then presents a searchable, filterable card browser.

ul.li: Full-text search across title, authors, abstract, DOI and journal
Citation counts and per-year sparklines from OpenAlex
Built-in PDF viewer with highlight and comment annotations, and click-through citation links that jump to the reference and back again
A viewer sidebar with the paper's table of contents, page thumbnails and your highlights
Structured full text (JATS XML) fetched from Europe PMC and stored beside the PDF, giving exact reference lists
Authors window: a persistent trail of the authors you follow, with their works, collaborators and affiliation history
Journal and topic subscriptions, flagging new papers by authors you have looked up before
BibTeX, RIS and CSL export; BibTeX and DOI import
Preprint detection (arXiv, bioRxiv, chemRxiv and more)
Duplicate detection by DOI and file hash, with supporting information recognised as belonging to its parent paper
An MCP server, so an AI assistant you already use can search and read your library — no model or API key inside the app
Sidecar JSON metadata lives next to each PDF, never inside it

description.p: A packaging fix. The AppStream metainfo file shipped with 0.4.0 was malformed and listed one of its releases twice, so software centres could not read it. No change to the application itself.
Alexandria now reads the publisher's own structured full text where a paper is open access, rather than recovering everything from the printed page.

ul.li: JATS full text fetched from Europe PMC and stored beside the PDF, giving exact reference lists — and a DOI for most references, so following a citation needs no search
The viewer shows the sentence a citation was made in, and can navigate back after a citation jump
A viewer sidebar with three modes: the paper's own table of contents, page thumbnails, and your highlights
Opening a paper no longer renders the whole paper first — a forty-page paper of micrographs took twenty seconds, and now takes under a second, whatever its length
Metadata is DOI-first: a resolved DOI supplies the record, and any disagreement with the PDF is flagged on the card rather than silently applied
"Find metadata" identifies older papers from a citation you can read off the page
Supporting information is linked to its parent paper instead of impersonating it
Papers can carry a summary, written by hand or by an AI assistant, always shown with its author or model
Subscriptions flag new papers by authors you follow
Bulk import no longer freezes the window: a folder of 185 PDFs went from multi-minute stalls to a few seconds
Authors window: one window with a persistent, reorderable trail of authors and a page for each, replacing the previous window-per-author
Author photos from Wikidata, a file, or dragged in from a web page
Collaborator cartouches: likely PI and group-member relationships inferred from shared publications
OpenAlex API-key support
Reference-lookup fixes
PDB accession codes on cards, linked to PDBe, with "Open in Coot" and drag-and-drop into Coot
Import from DOI, and a Discover tab that finds papers by PDB code
An MCP server, so an AI assistant you already use can search and read the library
Embedded terminal pane
Funding, licence, open-access and Crossmark information on cards
Multiple catalogues
